why: The whole of issue #428, put back. A page that has shown nobody anything owns a canvas, a renderer, a GL context, a simulation world, a gameplay seed and a frame loop again, and a player who opens the game and walks away pays for a match they never asked for. 41 of 66 in the scoped run, and the breadth is the point rather than a nuisance: the eager start is not one behaviour but the premise every session-shaped assertion in boot.test.ts used to rest on, so re-adding it breaks the empty-boot counts, every start-gesture count (each reads one session too many), and the whole reboot ledger. The narrow half is 'reaches the application UI with no session, no canvas and no world', which is the one that would fail even if every other case were rewritten around it. COUNT RE-MEASURED for issue #429 on the final tree: main's 34 of 58 -> 41 of 66. boot.test.ts gains the eight-test return-to-routes suite, and seven of those eight fail under an eager start; the eighth asserts only that the page owners survive, which the mutation does not touch. The failing set was decomposed, not renumbered: 34 of the 41 name tests that exist unchanged on main, and 7 are the new suite's. main declares 34, so the pre-existing count is unchanged; individual pre-existing verdicts were not re-measured on main's tree. An earlier 39 recorded on this branch matched no tree it shipped on -- CI and a local re-run both measure 41. COUNT RE-MEASURED for issue #685: 41 -> 43, with the failing SET decomposed. The two additions are the new replacement-failure suite's `draws the recoverable overlay over the working shell, and reports the original once` and `Retry restarts the SAME descriptor on a fresh canvas`. Both count sessions and canvases from a start, which an eager boot session shifts. Its FATAL case asserts the page and passes. COUNT RE-MEASURED for issue #690: 43 -> 47 of 87, with the failing SET decomposed. The 43 failures outside the new suite are unchanged in number. The four additions are all in `boot: an uncaught error during a running match (issue #690)`: `stops the session and draws the match-failed overlay, reporting the error once`, `routes an unhandled rejection the same way`, `reports a failure once, however many events it raises, and nothing with no session running`, and `does not report again a failed start that boot already handled`. Each counts disposals, errors or sessions from a single gesture, which an eager boot session shifts. Its message-fallback and page-teardown cases pass.
